To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of an unbounded operator are real analytic or quasianalytically differentiable with respect to the operator parameter, if and only if the resolvent is so.
the spectrum and eigenfunctions of a family of unbounded operators are CM-smooth with respect to the parameter.

the eigenvalues of the perturbation A(t) of the unperturbed operator A0 are CM-differentiable in t if the resolvents of the unperturbated operator A0 and of the perturbated operator A(t) are CM-differentible in t.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a perturbation theory for unbounded operators with CM-dependent domain of definition.
the CM-dependence of eigenvalue problems.
the perturbative behavior of eigenvalues and eigenspaces under a CM-mapping $${t\to A(t)}$$ of unbounded operators with common domain of definition, which are self- adjoint or normal.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the perturbation of a self-adjoint (or normal) operator A0 in a Denjoy–Carleanly differentiable direction is also a normal (self-adjoint) operator.
the perturbations of the eigenvectors and the eigenvalues are CM-differentiable in t, provided that the eigenvalues are simple and that the eigenvectors are CM-differentible.
the eigenvectors of a CM-mapping of self-adjoint operators are CM-dependent on the parameter.
